TF-PIM-001 Wave E — selftest harness coverage for the App token-exchange failure mode (TF-PIM-001-ARCH-002). This is the same-PR Wave D coupling per impl WP plan-doc §4 Wave E + Wave D R2 ARCH-MIN-002 closure + the operator-decided sequential sequencing captured in the Wave D dispatch JSON's `notes` field.

THIS IS A TIER 2 KERNEL-DANGEROUS FEDERATION-PRIMITIVE CHANGE. Touch only these three files:
- `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml` (Wave E adds 1 workflow_call input + 1 env-mapping + 1 new step BEFORE Wave D's token-exchange step)
- `.github/workflows/workflow-selftest.yml` (Wave E adds 1 new reusable-workflow invocation job + extends the orchestrator `workflow-selftest` job's `needs:` + adds an assertion that the simulated-failure job result is `failure` or `cancelled` + updates the `validate-selftest-config` count guard from `!= 2` to `!= 3`)
- `tests/workflow/conftest.md` (Wave E appends a paragraph documenting the new fixture + the v0.1-mock-based-coverage decision rationale + the TF-PIM-001-ARCH-002 real-API follow-up tracker; ALSO updates the existing stale paragraph about SHA-pinning convention)

**PRECONDITION (machine-enforced via verify_commands 0-1; aborts hard before any edit if violated):** Wave D dispatch has already fired + committed onto this branch. Wave D's edits to `policy-check.yml` are present in the working tree: (a) the token-exchange step `Obtain SCP federation App installation token` exists with `id: scp-app-token` + `if: github.action_ref != ''` + `uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0`; (b) EDIT 2 line `token: ${{ steps.scp-app-token.outputs.token }}` is present on the `.scp-runtime` checkout; (c) EDIT 3 line `token: ${{ steps.scp-app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}` is present on the `_scp-workflow` schema-lookup checkout. Wave E ASSUMES this state and extends it. If any Wave D artefact is missing, ABORT — Wave E's edits depend on Wave D's structural anchors.

# Required edits

## EDIT 1 — Add `simulate-app-token-failure` workflow_call input to policy-check.yml

In `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml`, under the `workflow_call.inputs:` block (currently containing 8 inputs: `rule-set`, `threshold`, `annotate`, `scp_bypass`, `waivers-path`, `rule-config-path`, `fixture-path`, `scorecard-emit`), append ONE new input definition. Place it AFTER `scorecard-emit:` (last input in the block, currently ending around line 54). Required YAML body:

```yaml
      simulate-app-token-failure:
        description: |
          Selftest-only flag (TF-PIM-001 Wave E / TF-PIM-001-ARCH-002 mock
          coverage). When true, a stub-mode step short-circuits the App
          installation token-exchange path: it emits the SCP-E001 annotation
          and exits 1 BEFORE the `actions/create-github-app-token` step
          runs. The SCP_TEST_SIMULATE_APP_TOKEN_FAILURE env-var is the
          conceptual name; the workflow input is the GitHub-Actions-native
          carrier. ONLY set true from the workflow-selftest harness;
          production callers leave this false. Blast radius if mis-set
          (accidentally or maliciously): the policy-check job fails on
          the caller's own PR; no other adopter is affected. Accidental
          mis-set is the more likely scenario.
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
```

Preserve all eight existing inputs verbatim. The new input is the NINTH (last) entry under `inputs:`. The 6-space indentation matches the existing input definitions.

## EDIT 2 — Add SCP_TEST_SIMULATE_APP_TOKEN_FAILURE env-mapping to policy-check.yml's job env

In `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml`, under `jobs.policy-check.env:` block (lines ~74-89), insert ONE new env-mapping. Insert immediately after `SCP_SUMMARY_PATH: policy-check-summary.json` (currently line ~85). The new line:

```yaml
      SCP_TEST_SIMULATE_APP_TOKEN_FAILURE: ${{ inputs.simulate-app-token-failure }}
```

The 6-space indentation matches the existing env-mappings. PRESERVE all 15 existing env-mappings verbatim (SCP_ANNOTATE, SCP_BASE_REF, SCP_BASE_SHA, SCP_BYPASS, SCP_BYPASS_APPROVED, SCP_HEAD_SHA, SCP_FIXTURE_PATH, SCP_PR_SHA, SCP_RULE_CONFIG_PATH, SCP_RULE_SET, SCP_SUMMARY_PATH, SCP_THRESHOLD, SCP_RUNTIME_ROOT, SCP_WAIVERS_PATH, SCP_WORKFLOW_RUN_ID). The new mapping is the SIXTEENTH.

## EDIT 3 — Insert the simulate-failure step BEFORE Wave D's token-exchange step in policy-check.yml

In `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml`, locate the Wave D step `- name: Obtain SCP federation App installation token` (added by Wave D; should be present at HEAD of this branch per PRECONDITION). Insert a NEW step IMMEDIATELY BEFORE it (sibling step at the same indentation; appears before the token-exchange step in execution order). Required YAML body (6 lines):

```yaml
      - name: Simulate App token-exchange failure (TF-PIM-001-ARCH-002 selftest fixture)
        if: ${{ inputs.simulate-app-token-failure }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::error file=.github/workflows/policy-check.yml,title=SCP-E001 (selftest)::Simulated App installation token-exchange failure (TF-PIM-001 Wave E mock fixture; inputs.simulate-app-token-failure=true). Production callers leave this input default-false."
          exit 1
```

The step:
- Has `if: ${{ inputs.simulate-app-token-failure }}` — runs ONLY when the input is true. Default false → step skipped → no behavior change for production callers.
- Fires REGARDLESS of `github.action_ref` (not co-gated with the token-exchange step). This is intentional: the selftest harness invokes `policy-check.yml` LOCALLY via `uses: ./...` (so `github.action_ref` is empty and the real token-exchange step naturally skips); the simulate step must fire independently of that guard to exercise the error-emission path under selftest.
- Emits `SCP-E001` workflow-command annotation with `file=.github/workflows/policy-check.yml` parameter matching the existing 16 SCP-E001 emission sites in this workflow (format consistency). The `(selftest)` title suffix distinguishes the test-only annotation from real infrastructure-failure SCP-E001 emissions for monitoring-adopter parsing. SCP-E001 reuse is semantically correct per ADOPT-001 §12.7.7 ("Infrastructure fetch failure" — App token-exchange IS an infrastructure failure mode the selftest is exercising).
- Exits 1, which fails the job. Subsequent steps (Wave D's token-exchange step + the `.scp-runtime` checkout + every downstream policy-check step) are SKIPPED by GitHub Actions' default step-failure cascade.
- Step is `run:`-only — contains NO `actions/checkout` and NO token parameter. The `persist-credentials: false` count of 3 (across the three existing checkout sites) is structurally preserved by construction; Wave E adds no fourth checkout.
- Step name explicitly tags `(TF-PIM-001-ARCH-002 selftest fixture)` so anyone reading the workflow knows it is a test-only hook.

## EDIT 4 — Add a third reusable-workflow invocation job in workflow-selftest.yml

In `.github/workflows/workflow-selftest.yml`, after the existing `fixture-fail-policy-check:` job (line ~196-226) and BEFORE the `workflow-selftest:` orchestrator job (line ~228), insert a NEW job. Required YAML body:

```yaml
  fixture-simulate-token-exchange-failure-policy-check:
    name: fixture-simulate-token-exchange-failure-policy-check
    needs: fixture-fail-policy-check
    permissions:
      contents: read
      statuses: write
    # TF-PIM-001 Wave E / TF-PIM-001-ARCH-002 selftest fixture. Invokes
    # the reusable workflow with simulate-app-token-failure=true, which
    # short-circuits the App token-exchange path: the simulate step emits
    # SCP-E001 and exits 1 BEFORE any real token-exchange API call. This
    # job's result is `failure` BY DESIGN — the orchestrator
    # `workflow-selftest` job asserts result ∈ {failure, cancelled} as
    # the success criterion (cancelled is acceptable under workflow-run
    # cancellation; same shape as the existing `Assert upstream job
    # outcomes are inspectable` step's treatment of fixture-fail-policy-check).
    # needs `fixture-fail-policy-check` for linear harness sequencing
    # (NOT for artifact-name conflict, which does not apply since this
    # job exits at the simulate step before any artifact-write step;
    # sequencing convention preserved for harness consistency).
    # v0.1 ships mock-based coverage; real-API coverage tracked-forward
    # as TF-PIM-001-ARCH-002 follow-up. See `tests/workflow/conftest.md`
    # for the mock-vs-real-API decision rationale.
    # Local reusable workflow: GitHub Actions runs this at the calling
    # workflow's HEAD SHA. `@<ref>` is not valid for local refs.
    uses: ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml
    with:
      fixture-path: tests/workflow/fixture-pass
      threshold: deny
      simulate-app-token-failure: true
```

The job reuses `tests/workflow/fixture-pass` as the fixture-path (no new fixture tree needed; the simulate step exits before fixture evaluation runs). The 2-space indentation under `jobs:` matches all other jobs.

## EDIT 5 — Extend the `workflow-selftest:` orchestrator job in workflow-selftest.yml

**EDIT 5a — Extend `needs:` block.** In the `workflow-selftest:` job (line ~228), replace:

```yaml
    needs:
      - stash-fixture-pass-summary
      - fixture-fail-policy-check
```

with:

```yaml
    needs:
      - stash-fixture-pass-summary
      - fixture-fail-policy-check
      - fixture-simulate-token-exchange-failure-policy-check
```

**EDIT 5b — Add an assertion step.** In the `workflow-selftest:` job's `steps:` list, insert a NEW step AFTER the existing `- name: Assert upstream job outcomes are inspectable` step and BEFORE the `- name: Compare reusable-workflow summaries to committed expectations` step. Required YAML body (11 lines):

```yaml
      - name: Assert simulate-token-exchange-failure job failed by design
        shell: bash
        env:
          SIMULATE_FAILURE_RESULT: ${{ needs.fixture-simulate-token-exchange-failure-policy-check.result }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [ "${SIMULATE_FAILURE_RESULT}" = "failure" ] || [ "${SIMULATE_FAILURE_RESULT}" = "cancelled" ] || {
            echo "::error::TF-PIM-001-ARCH-002 selftest: simulate-token-exchange-failure job must result in 'failure' (got '${SIMULATE_FAILURE_RESULT}'). The simulate step is expected to emit SCP-E001 and exit 1 (failure = by-design success criterion); cancelled is acceptable under workflow-run cancellation; any other outcome means the failure-path wiring is broken."
            exit 1
          }
```

The assertion treats `failure` as by-design success, `cancelled` as acceptable (upstream cancellation propagation; matches the established `Assert upstream job outcomes are inspectable` treatment for `fixture-fail-policy-check`), and any other outcome (`success`, `skipped`, etc.) as a wiring break. The 6-space indentation matches sibling steps in the `workflow-selftest:` job.

## EDIT 6 — Update conftest.md (append new content + replace stale paragraph)

**EDIT 6a — Replace stale SHA-pinning paragraph.** In `tests/workflow/conftest.md`, locate the existing paragraph that begins "The selftest pins `policy-check.yml` to the latest commit on this branch that changed `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml`. Any PR that changes that workflow must update both pinned `uses:` lines in `workflow-selftest.yml` to that commit SHA; the preflight job enforces this." Replace it with:

```
The selftest invokes `policy-check.yml` as a local reusable workflow (`uses: ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml` without `@<ref>`). GitHub Actions does NOT support `@<ref>` for local reusable-workflow `uses:` lines (only cross-repo refs accept `@ref`); local workflows always run at the calling workflow's HEAD SHA. No pin update is needed on `workflow-selftest.yml` when `policy-check.yml` changes. The `validate-selftest-config` preflight job verifies the invocation count (currently three: fixture-pass, fixture-fail, fixture-simulate-token-exchange-failure) and the per-PR diff-based oracle ratchet instead.
```

Rationale: the existing paragraph describes a SHA-pinning convention that was abandoned per WP-SCP-022 020C.1 follow-up (GitHub Actions does NOT support `@<ref>` on local reusable-workflow `uses:` lines). The replacement reflects the current convention.

**EDIT 6b — Append two new paragraphs at the END of conftest.md.** After the existing last paragraph (about fixture-fail ratcheting), append:

```
## TF-PIM-001 Wave E — simulate-token-exchange-failure fixture (mock-based)

TF-PIM-001 Wave E (TF-PIM-001-ARCH-002) adds a third reusable-workflow invocation to this harness: `fixture-simulate-token-exchange-failure-policy-check`. The invocation passes `simulate-app-token-failure: true` to `policy-check.yml`, which engages a stub-mode step that emits an `SCP-E001` workflow-command annotation (with `(selftest)` title suffix) and exits 1 BEFORE the real `actions/create-github-app-token` step runs. The selftest asserts the invocation's result is `failure` or `cancelled` (same by-design-failure shape as the `fixture-fail-policy-check` job; cancelled is acceptable under workflow-run cancellation). The fixture-path input is reused from `tests/workflow/fixture-pass` — no new fixture tree is required because the simulate step exits before fixture evaluation runs.

**Mock-vs-real-API decision (TF-PIM-001 impl WP plan-doc v0.4 §4 Wave E strategic-review decision):** v0.1 ships mock-based coverage only. The mock-mode flag is sufficient to verify the workflow's error-path code is wired correctly — that the simulate step emits SCP-E001 and that the workflow fails when the App token-exchange path is broken. Real-API coverage (exercising a real test App with an intentionally-broken installation, calling the real GitHub App API, verifying the actual failure mode) is tracked-forward as a TF-PIM-001-ARCH-002 follow-up. Real-API coverage is out-of-scope for this WP; it lands as a separate impl slice once TF-PIM-001 closes and Wave H restores PIM `main`'s required-check. The mock-based approach is deterministic in CI (no external GitHub App API dependency), simpler to author + test, and adequate as v0.1 of the selftest fixture.
```

PRESERVE all other existing conftest.md content above the EDIT 6a target paragraph (fixture-pass / fixture-fail descriptions, oracle ratchet paragraph, etc.).

## EDIT 7 — Update `validate-selftest-config` count guard in workflow-selftest.yml

In `.github/workflows/workflow-selftest.yml`, locate the `validate-selftest-config` job's inline Python heredoc (lines ~36-97). Change TWO lines:

== Same-PR coupling with Wave D ==
Wave E lands on the SAME PR BRANCH as Wave D (per Wave D R2 ARCH-MIN-002 closure + the operator-decided sequential sequencing). Wave D dispatches FIRST + commits; Wave E dispatches SECOND + commits on top. Both changesets land in the PR BEFORE merge. == Plan-doc divergence: env-var → workflow_call input ==
The impl WP plan-doc v0.4 §4 Wave E Action step 2 reads `Add the SCP_TEST_SIMULATE_APP_TOKEN_FAILURE env-var flag check at the top of the token-exchange step in policy-check.yml; when set, exit with SCP-E001 annotation immediately`. The plan-doc envisions an ENV-VAR. The dispatch JSON IMPLEMENTS this as a workflow_call INPUT + env-mapping pair because GitHub Actions does NOT propagate caller-scope env: declarations into reusable workflows (only inputs propagate). The mapping is: new workflow_call input `simulate-app-token-failure` (boolean, default false) → job-level env `SCP_TEST_SIMULATE_APP_TOKEN_FAILURE: ${{ inputs.simulate-app-token-failure }}` (preserves plan-doc env-var naming for downstream-step access) → simulate step's `if: ${{ inputs.simulate-app-token-failure }}` gate. The plan-doc §4 Wave E Action step 2 should receive a post-R-fixpoint hygiene amendment to capture the env-var-vs-input mechanism explicitly (operator-paced; out-of-scope for this dispatch). Plan-doc §4 Wave E Action step 5 also references `tests/workflow-selftest/README.md` which does not exist; the actual path is `tests/workflow/conftest.md` — another post-R-fixpoint hygiene amendment candidate.

== SCP-E001 annotation surface preservation ==
Wave E emits SCP-E001 from the simulate step. ADOPT-001 §12.7.7 defines SCP-E001 as "Infrastructure fetch failure" (OPA/Conftest binary unreachable, SHA256 mismatch, lockfile pin missing, App token-exchange failure). The App token-exchange failure mode IS an infrastructure failure semantically — Wave E exercises this failure path under simulation, so SCP-E001 reuse is correct, not a new code. The (selftest) title suffix + `file=` parameter match the existing 16 SCP-E001 emission sites' format conventions for monitoring-adopter distinguishability. D-050 §Justification invariant 5 ("Annotation surface is fixed") fully preserved: no new SCP-EXXX code introduced.

== Wave E v0.1 mock-based coverage (per plan-doc strategic-review decision) ==
The simulate step short-circuits the token-exchange path by emitting SCP-E001 + exiting 1 BEFORE the real `actions/create-github-app-token` step runs. DETERMINISTIC in CI (no external GitHub App API dependency), SIMPLE to author + test, SUFFICIENT to verify the workflow's error-path code is wired correctly.

Real-API coverage (exercising a real test App with an intentionally-broken installation) is tracked-forward as TF-PIM-001-ARCH-002 follow-up per plan-doc §9. Out-of-scope for this WP; lands as a separate impl slice once TF-PIM-001 closes + Wave H restores PIM main's required-check.
